question.worked_solution:
If we let $u=4{x}^{2},$ then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=8x\,⟹\,\text{d}u=8x\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives

| $x$ | $0$ | $\sqrt{\pi /4}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $\pi $ |

Using the above, we can rewrite the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi /4}}8x\operatorname{cos}⁡(4{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi /4}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4{x}^{2})\cdot 8x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(u)\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(u)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0) \\  & =0-0 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$
